question: When next-token data are generated by multiple latent stochastic factors, do transformers spontaneously encode the factors in low-dimensional, mutually orthogonal residual-stream subspaces, and do they prefer that geometry even when factorization loses predictive information?

key_findings.claim: For conditionally independent generalized-HMM factors, the joint predictive state remains on a product-state manifold and admits a lossless lower-dimensional representation by its factor marginals.
key_findings.evidence: If the initial predictive state and every token-labeled transition factor as tensor products, belief updates preserve product states. A linear marginalization map sends the joint state to the direct sum of local predictive vectors and is one-to-one when restricted to that product manifold. The joint ambient affine dimension is (product_n d_n)-1, whereas the factored intrinsic dimension is sum_n(d_n-1); reconstructing the joint state by tensoring marginals is nonlinear.

anchors.section: 2.2-2.3 Predictive vectors and conditionally independent generators
A.3 Joint representation and product-state submanifold
A.4-A.5 Factored representation and joint-to-factored map

key_findings.claim: The theorem establishes that a factored coordinate system exists; it does not make orthogonal factor axes a necessary or identifiable consequence of next-token loss.
key_findings.evidence: Marginalization is a lossless coordinate map on product states, and the paper chooses injections that place each marginal in a direct-sum block that can be made orthogonal. But any invertible mixing of those coordinates can preserve all predictions while changing Euclidean angles. The Factored World Hypothesis is therefore an additional inductive-bias hypothesis, not a consequence of Theorem 2.3 alone.

key_findings.claim: On five independent factors, the final transformer residual stream is much closer to the predicted 10-dimensional factored geometry than to the high-dimensional joint reference.
key_findings.evidence: The opaque-token generator combines three Mess3 and two Bloch Walk factors into a 432-token vocabulary. The joint predictive representation varies in 242 dimensions, while the direct sum varies in 10. The 4-layer, 3-head, d_model=120 model starts near 100 dimensions at the 95% cumulative-explained-variance threshold, compresses below 10, and plateaus around 11; the paper's 95%-variance joint reference is about 135 components. Linear regressions visually reconstruct all five marginal predictive geometries with low RMSE.

anchors.section: C.1.3-C.2 Joint and independent process construction

key_findings.claim: The orthogonality result is approximate, and one of its two advertised mathematical diagnostics contains a proof-level error.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix H.2.1 states that dim(A+B)=dim(A)+dim(B) implies A∩B={0}, 'i.e.' orthogonality. Trivial intersection does not imply Euclidean orthogonality: two skew one-dimensional lines can intersect only at zero while having a non-right angle. Effective-dimension additivity can diagnose shared exact directions, not principal angles. Only the separate basis-invariant overlap metric in H.2.2 directly measures geometric orthogonality, and the main text reports that overlap drops markedly mainly for the first two PCs.

key_findings.claim: Several reported quantities are close to, but do not exactly equal, the paper's ideal 10-dimensional mutually orthogonal prediction.
key_findings.evidence: The independent residual stream plateaus at 11 rather than 10 dimensions at 95% CEV. The learned embedding has around 12 non-negligible singular values. The sum of factor-specific effective dimensions remains about 14 while their union is about 12 in the plotted analysis, and Appendix Figure 15 says the two Bloch Walk factors require four PCs each to reach 95% variance even though their intrinsic predictive geometry is two-dimensional. These are compatible with approximate concentration, not exact direct-sum recovery.

anchors.section: D.6 Factoring starts at the embedding matrix

key_findings.claim: A dependency chain that preserves conditional independence also produces low-dimensional marginal geometry, but the paper does not repeat the strongest vary-one orthogonality test there.
key_findings.evidence: In a chain where each factor's transition variant depends on earlier emitted subtokens but the total token-labeled operator remains a tensor product, effective dimension collapses to 10 and linear probes recover all factor predictive vectors. Appendix H notes that vary-one sampling is not available for conditionally dependent factors and substitutes regression coefficient subspaces, while the main dependent-chain result emphasizes dimension and reconstruction rather than the full independent-case overlap trajectory.

key_findings.claim: Under token corruption, models transiently pass through a low-dimensional regime before expanding as the factor approximation becomes more lossy.
key_findings.evidence: For ε from 0 to 0.5, a memoryless channel makes predictive states leave the product manifold. The CEV trajectories first approach the factored scale; at ε≤0.05 they remain close, whereas at ε≥0.1 the curves soften and use more dimensions. The authors interpret this dwell-and-depart pattern as a factored representational attractor under later loss pressure.

key_findings.claim: The corruption experiment does not quantify the claimed fidelity sacrifice or causally isolate factorization from generic low-rank learning dynamics.
key_findings.evidence: The paper provides CEV-over-training plots but no Bayes-optimal cross-entropy, constrained factored-decoder loss, projection KL, or matched low-rank nonfactored control at each ε. An early 10-dimensional phase could arise from spectral bias or generally simpler features rather than a preference for the specific factor marginals. Linear marginal probes show accessibility, but no intervention forces or removes the candidate subspaces and measures the corresponding loss gap.

key_findings.claim: Low-dimensional PCA plus accurate marginal probes does not rule out nonlinear or low-variance joint information.
key_findings.evidence: CEV counts only the components carrying a chosen percentage of activation variance, here primarily 95%. The regressions target concatenated factor marginals, not the full 242-dimensional joint predictive state or cross-factor correlations. A model may place interaction information in low-variance directions or encode it nonlinearly while still allowing excellent linear recovery of marginals; no constrained decoder or full-joint probe tests this alternative.

key_findings.claim: The regression protocol and uncertainty reporting are insufficient for a strong quantitative decoding claim.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix G uses 10-fold cross-validation to select an SVD rcond threshold, then fits the final regression on all data and reports RMSE; a held-out final test RMSE and numeric per-factor table are not supplied. Most curves appear to be single training trajectories without seed intervals. Figure 3's 90% band covers an ensemble of random initializations for overlap, not uncertainty across trained models.

anchors.section: G.1-G.3 Least squares, SVD threshold, and RMSE

key_findings.claim: RNN and LSTM controls weaken a transformer-specific interpretation while supplying a useful negative result about sharpness.
key_findings.evidence: A d_model=32 vanilla RNN also reaches roughly 10 components for 95% variance and linearly exposes all five factors. At d_model=64 it settles around 16, and LSTMs smooth earlier; even a d_model=256 RNN remains closer to the factored than joint reference. The authors leave open whether architectural differences reflect optimization dynamics or inductive bias.

anchors.section: D.4 Experiments with RNNs and LSTMs

key_findings.claim: The synthetic observation interface contains no explicit subtoken factor labels, but the experiment remains unusually favorable to marginal recovery and is far from evidence about natural-language models.
key_findings.evidence: Five generated subtokens are bijectively packed into one of 432 opaque token IDs, and the factors are selected so their predictive vectors determine their next-subtoken distributions. This is a meaningful latent-discovery test, yet it gives exact generators, factor targets, and controlled vary-one data to the analyst. The conclusion explicitly frames extrapolation to larger models and unsupervised discovery tools as plausible future work rather than demonstrated transfer.

key_findings.claim: The main text and appendix give inconsistent definitions of the noisy channel.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.3 says an emitted token is replaced with a uniformly random token with probability ε, which permits drawing the original token. Appendix C.4 instead says it is replaced uniformly by any other token and Equation 33 normalizes by |X|-1. The difference is small for a 432-token vocabulary but changes the exact transition operator and stated interpretation of ε.

method.core_idea: Derive competing joint-versus-factored predictive-state geometries from product-structured generalized HMMs, then train sequence models on opaque tokens from known synthetic factors and compare residual-stream dimensionality, factor decodability, and factor-subspace angles with those predictions.
method.mechanism: Token-labeled GHMM operators propagate normalized predictive vectors. Tensor-product operators preserve a product-state manifold, whose factor marginals can be concatenated in a direct sum using exponentially fewer intrinsic dimensions than the joint ambient state. Experiments combine three Mess3 and two Bloch Walk factors into 432 opaque tokens, train GPT-2-style transformers, and analyze final-block residuals using cumulative explained variance and SVD linear regression. Vary-one datasets isolate candidate factor subspaces; effective-dimension comparisons and principal-angle overlap assess their organization. A dependency chain preserves product structure, while a token-noise channel breaks it to test whether training temporarily favors the cheaper marginal geometry.
assumptions: The predictive vector is the task-relevant latent state for optimal next-token prediction and is identifiable up to a useful geometric transform in activations.
Variance-dominant linear structure in the selected final-block residual location captures the representation used by the model.
A 95% CEV threshold is a meaningful proxy for effective dimension and is qualitatively stable over thresholds from 90% to 99%.
Accurate linear reconstruction of each marginal predictive vector indicates that its geometry is explicitly represented.
Vary-one mean-centering removes fixed-factor contributions sufficiently well to isolate one factor's subspace.
Principal-angle overlap of the selected PCA or regression bases reflects functional separation of factor information.
The synthetic GHMM factors and opaque Cartesian-product tokens expose an inductive bias relevant beyond the chosen generators.
Training trajectories and reported initialization ensembles are representative despite limited trained-seed uncertainty.

techniques.role: Maps contexts to sufficient predictive vectors whose arrangement supplies explicit representational targets.
Constructs a lossless low-dimensional direct-sum coordinate system for conditionally independent factors.
Hides five latent subtokens behind one integer token so the network must infer factor structure from sequence statistics.
Tracks the number of residual-stream PCs needed to explain a fixed fraction of variance over training.
Tests whether all factor marginals can be reconstructed from activations by SVD-regularized least squares.
Holds four generated factor sequences fixed and varies one to estimate its activation subspace.
Computes a basis-invariant normalized Frobenius overlap between pairs of candidate factor subspaces.
Separates dependence compatible with product belief updates from corruption that makes a factored predictive state lossy.

evaluations.setting: Four-layer, three-head, d_model=120 transformer on five independent latent factors packed into 432 opaque tokens
evaluations.metric: Components required for 95% residual-stream cumulative explained variance
evaluations.result: The trajectory begins near 100, dips below 10, and plateaus around 11 dimensions
evaluations.baseline: Factored prediction 10 dimensions; joint-state 95%-variance reference about 135 and full ambient variation 242

evaluations.metric: Linear regression RMSE and qualitative reconstruction of five predictive geometries
evaluations.result: All five marginal geometries are recovered with visually low error, but no consolidated held-out numeric RMSE table is reported
evaluations.baseline: Ground-truth Mess3 and Bloch Walk predictive vectors

evaluations.setting: Vary-one datasets for the five independent factors

evaluations.result: The sum approaches about 14 versus a union around 12, while overlap falls strongly mainly for the first two PCs of each pair
evaluations.baseline: Exact orthogonal direct sum would have additive exact dimensions and zero pairwise overlap

evaluations.metric: Singular spectrum and PCA arrangement by hidden subtoken

evaluations.setting: Two-layer vanilla RNNs and LSTMs on the independent process

limitations: Author-stated: the theory predicts a lossless factored representation only when belief updates preserve product states; otherwise factor marginalization discards cross-factor predictive information.
Author-stated: vary-one analysis requires independent generative factors and cannot be applied directly to the conditional-dependency chain.
Author-stated: whether RNN/transformer differences arise from architecture, training dynamics, or inductive bias remains open.
Author-stated: extrapolation to larger natural-language models and unsupervised discovery of factor subspaces is plausible but untested.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem 2.3 proves existence of a lossless direct-sum coordinate map, not that optimization must choose orthogonal axes or that the learned factorization is identifiable.
Reviewer-identified: Appendix H.2.1 incorrectly equates trivial subspace intersection with orthogonality, invalidating effective-dimension additivity as direct angle evidence.
Reviewer-identified: 95%-CEV counts, marginal linear probes, and approximate principal angles do not exclude nonlinear or low-variance joint information.
Reviewer-identified: no constrained factored baseline, Bayes-optimal loss, projection KL, or causal ablation quantifies how much fidelity the noisy models sacrifice in their low-rank phase.
Reviewer-identified: trained-seed uncertainty, numeric RMSE tables, and a final held-out regression evaluation are absent or limited.
Reviewer-identified: the result is restricted to small synthetic GHMMs and opaque Cartesian-product tokens whose factor targets are exactly available to the analyst.
Reviewer-identified: position, BOS, and other nuisance variation is not explicitly regressed out and may contribute to the observed 11-12 dimensions versus the ideal 10.
Reviewer-identified: the noisy-channel definition differs between Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4.
failure_modes: A low-variance but causally essential cross-factor feature can be missed by the 95%-CEV threshold and falsely classified as absent.
An invertible rotation can mix factor coordinates without changing predictions, making Euclidean orthogonality a basis-dependent training artifact rather than a functional invariant.
Vary-one mean-centering can retain interaction directions whose form depends on the fixed factors when the network representation is nonlinear and nonadditive.
Linear probes can recover correlated targets from shared directions and therefore overstate separation unless combined with interventions or exclusivity tests.
Selecting an SVD threshold by cross-validation and refitting on all observations can make reported reconstruction error optimistic without a held-out test set.
Position embeddings, BOS tokens, and context-index effects can inflate apparent dimension or create shared subspace overlap unrelated to latent factors.
Generic low-rank or spectral learning bias can mimic an early factored attractor in the noisy experiment without representing the intended marginals.
Natural-language factors may be dependent, nonstationary, nonidentifiable, and hierarchically overlapping, so the clean direct-sum geometry may not transfer.
At finite CEV thresholds, sums and unions of effective dimensions do not obey the exact subspace dimension identity used in the appendix.
reusable_insights: Translate latent conditional-independence assumptions into explicit competing activation geometries before probing a trained network.
Use opaque composite tokens to test whether factor structure is discovered from temporal statistics rather than handed to the embedding interface.
Separate existence of a compact sufficient representation from an optimizer's preference for a particular coordinate basis.
Combine dimension, decoding, pairwise angles, causal ablation, and predictive fidelity; no single geometric diagnostic establishes factorization.
Stress-test a representational hypothesis where it becomes suboptimal, then quantify both how long training retains it and the loss paid for doing so.
Treat exact subspace dimension identities cautiously when dimensions are estimated by arbitrary variance thresholds.
Use architecture controls to distinguish a transformer-specific bias from a generic neural optimization trajectory.
open_questions: Does projecting out or ablating each identified factor subspace selectively impair only that factor's predictions?
How much cross-entropy or predictive KL is lost by an explicitly constrained factored decoder at every noise level and training step?
Do factor subspaces remain identifiable under invertible rotations, correlated emissions, unequal factor entropy, or alternative token encodings?
Can nonlinear full-joint probes detect cross-factor information hidden outside the variance-dominant marginal subspaces?
Are the 11-12 observed dimensions explained by positions, BOS, two extra Bloch-Walk PCs, or genuine interaction structure?
Which optimizer, initialization, or architecture features cause transformers to factor more sharply than the tested RNNs and LSTMs?
Can unsupervised methods recover factor number and subspaces in natural-language or multimodal foundation models without generator access?
What basis-invariant functional notion should replace raw orthogonality when representations are equivalent under invertible mixing?

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
competitive_landscape.difference: Shai et al. already show that transformer residual streams linearly represent GHMM predictive-state geometry. The target extends that program from one latent process to tensor-product processes and asks whether marginal geometries occupy separate subspaces, so the novelty is factor decomposition and the noisy preference experiment rather than belief geometry itself.

competitive_landscape.title: From monoliths to modules: Decomposing transducers for efficient world modelling
competitive_landscape.difference: Boyd et al. formalize when stochastic transducers decompose into modular components and how such modules reduce world-model complexity. The target studies whether ordinary neural sequence models spontaneously realize an analogous direct-sum predictive geometry; its empirical subspace evidence is new relative to the transducer decomposition but less general mathematically.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural networks leverage nominally quantum and post-quantum representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Riechers et al. introduce the Bloch-Walk-style generalized predictive representations used here and show transformers and RNNs can exploit compact quantum/post-quantum geometries. The target composes five such generators and tests marginal factor organization; it inherits rather than originates the unusual factor geometries.

competitive_landscape.title: Constrained belief updates explain geometric structures in transformer representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Piotrowski et al. connect attention, embeddings, and OV circuits to constrained Bayesian belief updates in synthetic transformers. The target offers a stronger factor-level geometric prediction across multiple processes but provides less circuit-level causal evidence for how the direct-sum organization is computed.

competitive_landscape.title: FACTS: A Factored State-Space Framework For World Modelling
competitive_landscape.difference: FACTS builds factorization into a structured state-space world model to separate objects and interactions. The target instead claims that an unmodified transformer discovers factors from opaque sequence statistics, but it tests small known generators rather than the richer object-centric world-model benchmarks and interventions used by engineered factor models.

competitive_landscape.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
competitive_landscape.difference: Engels et al. demonstrate irreducibly multidimensional feature manifolds in real language models and validate them with interventions. The target supplies exact predicted dimensions and between-factor relationships in synthetic models, but its orthogonality claims are primarily correlational and its natural-language extrapolation is untested.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that next-token-trained transformers learn to decompose a latent world into parts represented in mutually orthogonal residual-stream subspaces, achieving exponential dimensional savings and showing a genuine preference for factorization even when it reduces predictive fidelity.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Product-GHMM theory gives an exact lossless marginal coordinate map under conditional independence. Across independent and dependency-chain synthetic data, PCA approaches the predicted 10-dimensional scale and marginal predictive vectors are linearly recoverable. Candidate factor overlaps fall during training, embeddings acquire subtoken structure, and noisy models transiently pass through the low-dimensional regime before expanding.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible new contribution is a controlled bridge from product predictive-state theory to training-time factor geometry, especially the opaque-token and off-manifold noise trajectories. It is not yet proof that transformers generally learn orthogonal world parts: belief-state geometry and multidimensional features are established priors; the direct-sum theorem is an existence result; Appendix H confuses trivial intersection with orthogonality; the empirical geometry is approximate; marginal PCA/probes do not exclude joint information; and neither the predictive cost nor causal function of the subspaces is measured. RNN results further narrow the claim from transformer-specific bias to a possibly broader optimization tendency.

reviewer_notes: The index-pinned 30-page extraction was read end to end, including every main-text figure and table, references, and every appendix A-I: complete GHMM/product-state derivations and joint-to-factored mapping (A), independent/dependent explicit examples and off-manifold information geometry (B), all Mess3/Bloch-Walk matrices and independent, chained, and noised generator definitions (C), every extended transformer, context, width, RNN/LSTM, noise, and embedding result (D), full architecture and optimization settings (E), CEV definitions and activation location (F), regression/SVD/cross-validation/RMSE details (G), both subspace-identification procedures and both orthogonality diagnostics (H), and the empirical synopsis (I). The artifact is the current arXiv:2602.02385v1 primary PDF; a fresh download checked 2026-08-23 matched indexed PDF SHA-256 d0582aa1da73f8f2ed7bf33b18ca246ed2acede27fb6dff9689e64a5ddcdd8db, and the cached extraction matched text SHA-256 796f2d782bcf5aa1ad92541e2bc7a522221ef50c76ba51e3526aa63cbd5859ee with 30/30 text-bearing pages. Six current direct competitors were checked at the exact primary arXiv versions recorded above on 2026-08-23. Author claims, author-stated scope, reviewer limitations, negative results, and internal contradictions are kept distinct. The highest-priority audit point is Appendix H.2.1's false equivalence between A∩B={0} and orthogonality; dimensional additivity cannot validate Euclidean orthogonality, so the claim must rest on the separate, approximate principal-angle evidence. The main-text statement that corruption selects a uniformly random token also conflicts with Appendix C.4's uniformly random other-token operator.
